methodologyRationale: Selected after efficient hyperparameter tuning across seven targeted XGBoost rank-model presets, followed by a four-fold confirmation run against the prior default.
The selected tuned preset uses shallower trees, a lower learning rate, and monthly train/validation sampling to reduce overfit risk from highly overlapping 252-trading-day labels.
A fixed 60 boosting rounds was chosen from walk-forward early-stopping diagnostics: it is close to the recent-fold median while staying below the highest fold-specific optimum.
The 15-year monthly training window remains the promoted long-horizon setup because it preserved more usable market history than the 10-year baseline without the weaker 20-year walk-forward profile.

Classic momentum baseline: 12-month performance excluding the most recent month.

Baseline that favors liquid, heavily traded stocks with lower volatility and lower illiquidity.
Simple baseline that favors lower 60-day realized volatility.

methodology: This is a separate long-horizon research model; it does not replace the 14-day tactical Momentum Book.
Monthly and quarterly medians are emphasized because daily 252D outcomes overlap heavily and averages can be skewed by outliers.
The promoted long-horizon artifact uses 15 years of labeled history, monthly train/validation sampling, and a compact tuned XGBoost rank model.
Baseline agreement labels compare the model with simple sector-relative and 12-1 momentum rules.
The drawdown-adjusted label is experimental until walk-forward results show it improves returns without only selecting low-volatility laggards.
Live one-year scores are refreshed from the same feature tape as the tactical model and are shown as a separate research lens.
The AI memo may use long-horizon results as supporting context; a single-name recommendation should rely on them only when tactical and long-horizon evidence both support the setup.
